chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from 'Abd Allah ibn Jabalah, from Muhammad ibn Mas'ud al-Ta'i, from 'Anbasah ibn Mus'ab, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said:
“Whoever receives a جنازة or sees it and says: Allah is the Greatest,
This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger have spoken the truth,

O Allah, increase us in faith and submission. All praise belongs to Allah, Who has manifested might through power and subdued the servants through death. There does not remain in the heaven any angel brought near except that he weeps in mercy at its sound.”

key_terms.إِيمَانًا: faith, meaning increased inner conviction in Allah's truth
key_terms.اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ: the formula of takbir, declaring Allah's supreme greatness
key_terms.الْمَوْتِ: death, described here as the means by which Allah subdues His servants
key_terms.تَسْلِيمًا: submission, meaning yielding obediently to Allah's decree
key_terms.جَنَازَةً: a funeral bier or corpse being carried for burial
key_terms.مَلَكٌ مُقَرَّبٌ: a near angel, one brought close to Allah in rank

ai.seo_question: What should be said when seeing or receiving a funeral bier in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a remembrance and du'a to be recited when encountering a جنازة, combining takbir, affirmation of divine promise, and praise of Allah's overpowering decree through death. It emphasizes death as a moment of reflection that deepens iman and submission, while also portraying the solemn cosmic mercy surrounding it.
